general_equity_assessment.title: General Equity Assessment for Policy Makers
general_equity_assessment.summary: The document illustrates an acknowledgment of the equity implications tied to water management, suggesting strengths and weaknesses in areas such as recognitional and structural equity.

recognitional_equity.title: Recognitional Equity
recognitional_equity.positive_findings: The document appears to recognize historical inequities in water access, particularly acknowledging the unique identities of marginalized communities.
recognitional_equity.concerns: While it mentions the need for tailored outreach, it does not provide specific examples of effective engagement strategies, suggesting potential gaps in recognition of diverse voices.
recognitional_equity.conclusion: Overall, there is a tentative indication of support for recognitional equity, albeit with room for more substantial engagement.

procedural_equity.title: Procedural Equity
procedural_equity.positive_findings: The emphasis on community-led engagement and procedural frameworks suggests a commitment to fair participation.
procedural_equity.concerns: The effectiveness of these frameworks remains uncertain as specific implementation strategies are not detailed, raising potential transparency issues.
procedural_equity.conclusion: While procedural equity is emphasized, there may be substantial gaps in actual practice.

distributional_equity.title: Distributional Equity
distributional_equity.positive_findings: There seems to be an intent to prioritize historically disadvantaged communities in resource allocation.
distributional_equity.concerns: However, concerns arise regarding the impacts of policies that might exacerbate existing disparities, particularly concerning environmental health.
distributional_equity.conclusion: The commitment to distributional equity is indicated, but with caution regarding implementation.

structural_equity.title: Structural Equity
structural_equity.positive_findings: The document recognizes systemic barriers affecting water access for disadvantaged communities.
structural_equity.concerns: The absence of actionable steps to dismantle these barriers may imply a shortage of comprehensive strategies towards structural change.
structural_equity.conclusion: While acknowledgment is a positive step, it points to a need for more effective plans to address deep-rooted inequities.
